clue.text: Fuel from seaweed wrapped in lettuce

indicators.note: the seaweed is enclosed by the lettuce, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: cos is a variety of long-leaved lettuce
alga is a single seaweed or pond plant

explanation.surface: A green energy story: fuel extracted from seaweed rolled up in lettuce leaves, like a salad wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal gas is a fuel made by heating coal, once piped to homes for lighting and cooking.

clue.text: Steps taken to get a pair of 21s?

definitions.note: plural dance steps standing for a single dance

indicators.note: a pair means two of the same thing, so one word is written twice

parts.note: the answer to 21 is a set of headphones, which are slangily called cans; one can each time

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a dance routine in order to earn a pair of something numbered 21.
explanation.walkthrough: '21s' points to the answer at 21 across, headphones, informally called cans.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking dance, a routine of steps from Parisian music halls.

clue.text: Actually it's really cool — starts working in car, and nothing needs to be taken off

definitions.text: in car, and nothing needs to be taken off

indicators.note: the starts of the first four words supply their opening letters

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A boast about a car's cooling: it works so well that nobody has to strip off layers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: with this running in a car, nobody needs to shed clothes to stay cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Air conditioning keeps a vehicle's cabin chilled, so passengers stay comfortable fully dressed.

clue.text: One grows sad — poor wife, she's missing husband

indicators.note: poor suggests a bad or broken state, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lonely wife grows miserable while her husband is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One grows' reads like a gardener or a plant; I, GROWS, SAD and W are all fodder for 'poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widow is a woman whose husband is away for long periods, for work or sport.

clue.text: Girl hasn't finished eating hot dish

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
the girl's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Susie is a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl leaves her plate half-eaten while tucking into a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't finished' cuts SUSIE to SUSI; 'eating' puts H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese preparation of vinegared rice, often with raw fish, served as a meal.

clue.text: Someone posting a few letters for one "doing bird"?

definitions.meaning: a user of a microblogging site, posting short messages of limited characters
a songbird making its call, i.e. chirping

explanation.surface: A short-message poster is compared to a jailed prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving prison time; here it is read literally as acting like a bird. The word is also a small loudspeaker, fitting the hi-fi theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A social-media user sends brief posts, and a songbird chirps; both senses come from the same verb.

clue.text: Ballerina eager initially to risk dancing in short ballet costume, a tight-fitting garment

indicators.note: the starts and the jumbled word go inside the shortened costume
the costume word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: a tutu is a ballerina's stiff skirt

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the two words
dancing suggests movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eager ballerina takes a risk, dancing in a skimpy ballet outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles 'risk' into SKIR; 'short' cuts the tutu to TUT, which goes round the rest via 'in'. The definition is the last phrase, not the ballet costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube skirt is a straight, stretchy, close-fitting skirt shaped like a tube.

clue.text: Love of Rolling Stones or Eagles

indicators.note: rolling suggests turning over, so the letters are read backwards
of signals letters taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A question of musical taste: a fondness for the Rolling Stones or the Eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE spans the end of 'Stones' and 'or' and the start of 'Eagles'; 'Rolling' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, so his name stands for desire itself.

clue.text: Topless group employed by bar, eliciting bit of a stern expression?

indicators.note: the group is placed next to the bar, as if working for it
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: staff is a group of employees
a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A topless troupe hired by a bar prompts a stern look from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' is the back of a ship, not a severe face; 'expression?' plays on 'stern expression'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail running round the stern of a ship.

clue.text: In the country band together after game

indicators.note: the band-together word follows the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to rally is to come together for a cause

explanation.surface: A rural scene: a band gathers to play after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band together' looks like a music group but is a verb; 'after' puts the game first. RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in a countryside manner or setting, away from towns.

clue.text: Opera stars, mostly French

definitions.meaning: a Bellini opera of this name
a small southern constellation, the Carpenter's Square

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: Norman French was the language of the Normans

explanation.surface: Opera stars, most of them from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes: Bellini's opera, the southern constellation, and NORMAN (as in Norman French) with its last letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's opera is named after its Druid priestess heroine; the constellation shares the name.

clue.text: A sound driver, this underdog?

definitions.meaning: a loudspeaker unit, or driver, reproducing low bass notes
read as sub (under) plus woofer (dog), an under-dog

explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is the speaker part, not a motorist; 'underdog' splits as sub (under) and woofer (barking dog).
explanation.definitionFit: A subwoofer is a loudspeaker dedicated to the lowest frequencies in a hi-fi setup.

clue.text: A surprised expression remains in the auditorium, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this asks for the words as heard rather than written

parts.note: a, then coo (an exclamation of surprise), then sticks (remains, stays put)

explanation.surface: A gasp of surprise lingers in a theatre, carried by the room's sound.
explanation.walkthrough: COO is a British exclamation of surprise; 'remains' is STICKS, as in stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics are the sound qualities of a hall, how well music and speech carry there.

clue.text: Current selection from 1994 album

indicators.note: a selection is a short run of letters taken from the middle of the words that follow, once spelt out

parts.note: the year written out in words, nineteen ninety-four, followed by album

explanation.surface: Picking one track from an album released in 1994.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 1994 out in words, nineteen ninety-four, and the letters sit across 'four album'. 'Current' is a river, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea, and a river is a current of water.

clue.text: Reviewing Elvis Costello, or Declan McManus originally, journalists make use of Chambers?

indicators.note: reviewing is taken as viewing again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
originally takes the first letter of each name word

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Journalists reviewing Elvis Costello, born Declan McManus, consult the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a famous dictionary, but here it means pressure chambers, used by divers to adjust safely. 'Reviewing' rearranges ECODM into DECOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers decompress in special chambers that reduce pressure gradually after a deep dive.

clue.text: Film made from a novel in good faith

definitions.meaning: a 2000 film from Nick Hornby's book about a record-shop owner
read literally as very loyal or faithful

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'high' as great and 'fidelity' as faithfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase also means sound reproduction faithful to the original, linking the hi-fi theme.

clue.text: That woman's a nasty thug, one intrinsically more arrogant

indicators.note: intrinsically means within, so the middle pieces go inside

parts.note: her is the possessive for that woman

indicators.note: nasty suggests something twisted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman's thug is a bully, and one with even more swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles 'a thug' into AUGHT, and 'intrinsically' sets that and the I inside 'That woman's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of haughty: prouder and more disdainful of others.

clue.text: Mix tape pile starts off covering Prince on piano? That's sweet

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the two single letters
mix suggests stirring together, so the letters are rearranged
the first letters of each word are removed

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A mixtape and a pile of records: a Prince track played on piano, a sweet result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' drops the T and P that begin 'tape' and 'pile'; 'Mix' rearranges APEILE around PP.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a classic baked dessert, a sweet in British usage for pudding.

clue.text: Discount's included for having children

indicators.note: the word for supports is placed inside the discount

parts.note: a reduction is a discount in price
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: A tax discount is given for having children.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' here is 'has': the discount has PRO included.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproduction is the biological process of producing offspring.

clue.text: Engineers drama in cup games?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
plays are drama

explanation.surface: Engineering some drama in cup competition matches.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: In knockout cup football, drawn ties are settled by rematches.

clue.text: Bit of bromide taken by randy model railway man

indicators.note: the bit is taken inside the randy word

parts.note: randy and horny both mean lustful

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Bromide, the old remedy for lust, is given to a randy model railway enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Bromide was reputed to dampen sexual desire, matching 'randy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Hornby founded the British firm famous for model trains.

clue.text: Bottom half of 14 commonly worn on bottom when retired?

indicators.note: the half and the letter are placed on, or inside, the bed

parts.note: after retiring for the night one is in bed

indicators.note: the first half of the short form is taken

parts.note: the answer at 14 is commonly shortened to hi-fi

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter is picked

explanation.surface: Something worn on one's backside when going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: '14 commonly' is hi-fi, and 'half of' it is HI; 'bottom' takes N from 'worn'. 'Bottom' first is the definition, the second an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The behind is the backside, a colloquial word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Group lost in small woofer

indicators.note: the letter for lost goes inside the small dog

parts.note: a pup is a young dog, a small barker
L is the abbreviation for lost in results tables

explanation.surface: A band disappears inside a small speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woofer' is a dog here, though nearby it is a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulp are a Sheffield rock band, a musical group.

clue.text: Capering after split is 26's alternative

parts.note: the word split, as 'after split' asks, into Cape and ring: a headland and a call on a telephone

explanation.surface: Frolicking about after a breakup, the loudspeaker's alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after split' tells you to divide 'Capering' into CAPE (a headland, so HEAD) and RING (call, so PHONE).
explanation.definitionFit: Listening through earpieces is the alternative to listening through a loudspeaker.

clue.text: Of all groups regularly entering Europe, top five are in concert

indicators.note: the tops of the next five words, one letter from each, are taken

explanation.surface: Of all the bands that tour Europe, the top five are playing at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' and 'entering' look like instructions but are just two of the five words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in concert is to act in harmony, holding the same view.

clue.text: Cut either half of 1D

definitions.meaning: half of the 1 down answer is can, slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: Can and nick are both British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A small notch or cut, and also British slang for a jail.

clue.text: Current long-term prisoner has one injected as booster

parts.note: amp is a unit of electric current

indicators.note: injected means put into, so the one goes inside

parts.note: a lifer is serving a life sentence
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A long-term prisoner is injected with a boost of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injected' puts I into LIFER.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts the strength of an electrical signal, as in a sound system.

clue.text: Feeling of weariness when performing No.1, some would say

indicators.note: signals the words as heard rather than written

parts.note: on (performing) plus wee (number one, child's word for urinating)

explanation.surface: Weariness felt while performing a chart-topping song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.1' is a child's euphemism for urinating, WEE; 'performing' is ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and dissatisfaction.

clue.text: Criminal keeps a revolver on either side of chair in house

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are jumbled
either side of the word revolver gives the same letter, since it begins and ends with it

explanation.surface: A criminal keeps a gun on either side of his chair at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' starts and ends with R, so 'on either side' supplies R; 'Criminal' jumbles KEEPS, A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker presides over the House of Commons, chairing its debates.

clue.text: Tried to bring back Purdey as sexy content

indicators.note: bring back means reverse, so the letters run the other way
content means what is inside the words

explanation.surface: An attempt to revive Purdey, from The New Avengers, as sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Purdey was the heroine of 1970s British TV series The New Avengers.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so essayed means attempted.
